50993171.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Keap1 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry
50993171.references_previous: M. Lu, H.-s. Zhou, Q.-D. You, Z. Jiang, Design, synthesis, and initial evaluation of affinity-based small-molecule probes for fluorescent visualization and specific detection of Keap1, J. Med. Chem. 59 (2016) 7305–7310.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC (isothermal: The assay was carried out as previously reported [53]. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) was performed at 25 °C with the ITC200 system (MicroCal). The Keap1 Kelch domain was lyophilized. Both the protein sample and the peptides were dissolved in 10 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.4). 2 μL aliquots of 0.05 mM peptide were injected 19 times at 2.5 min intervals from a stirring syringe (750 rpm) into the sample cell containing 220 μL of 0.005 mM Keap1 Kelch domain. Data were analyzed with the computer program Origin, version 7.0, supplied by MicroCal.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. ITC titration profiles of Keap1 Kelch Domain with peptides and thermodynamic parameters of the interaction with Keap1 of peptides determined by ITC assay.
original_paragraph.Table in Figure 2: Thermodynamic parameters of the interactions with Keap1 of peptides determined by ITC Assay No. Sequence N Kd (nM) ΔH (kcal·mol⁻¹) TΔS (kcal·mol⁻¹) ΔG (kcal·mol⁻¹) Mw (Da) Peptide 4 Ac-GQLDPETGEFL-OH 1.03 ± 0.02 86.96 -19.22 -9.57 -9.65 1247.33 Peptide 3 c[GQLDPETGEFL] 1.05 ± 0.03 18.12 -18.35 -7.78 -10.57 1187.20 *N is the stoichiometric coefficient. Kd is the binding constant. ΔH, ΔS, and ΔG refer to the changes in binding enthalpy, entropy, and total Gibbs free energy, respectively. ΔG is calculated according to the equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, with T the absolute temperature set up for the ITC experiment.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 ITC thermograms: The ITC thermograms for Peptide 4 and Peptide 3 are shown in Figure 2. The upper panels show the heat flow (μcal/sec) over time (min). The lower panels show the integrated heat (kcal/mol of injectant) versus the molar ratio of peptide to Keap1. For Peptide 4, the molar ratio ranges from 0.0 to 2.0. For Peptide 3, the molar ratio ranges from 0.0 to 1.5.

50993152.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human Keap1 Kelch domain (322 to 609 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli (DE3) by isothermal titration calorimetry
50993152.references_previous: M. Lu, H.-s. Zhou, Q.-D. You, Z. Jiang, Design, synthesis, and initial evaluation of affinity-based small-molecule probes for fluorescent visualization and specific detection of Keap1, J. Med. Chem. 59 (2016) 7305–7310.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC (isothermal: The assay was carried out as previously reported [53]. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) was performed at 25 °C with the ITC200 system (MicroCal). The Keap1 Kelch domain was lyophilized. Both the protein sample and the peptides were dissolved in 10 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.4). 2 μL aliquots of 0.05 mM peptide were injected 19 times at 2.5 min intervals from a stirring syringe (750 rpm) into the sample cell containing 220 μL of 0.005 mM Keap1 Kelch domain. Data were analyzed with the computer program Origin, version 7.0, supplied by MicroCal.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. ITC titration profiles of Keap1 Kelch Domain with peptides and thermodynamic parameters of the interaction with Keap1 of peptides determined by ITC assay.
original_paragraph.Table in Figure 2: Thermodynamic parameters of the interactions with Keap1 of peptides determined by ITC Assay No. Sequence N Kd (nM) ΔH (kcal·mol⁻¹) TΔS (kcal·mol⁻¹) ΔG (kcal·mol⁻¹) Mw (Da) Peptide 4 Ac-GQLDPETGEFL-OH 1.03 ± 0.02 86.96 -19.22 -9.57 -9.65 1247.33 Peptide 3 c[GQLDPETGEFL] 1.05 ± 0.03 18.12 -18.35 -7.78 -10.57 1187.20 *N is the stoichiometric coefficient. ΔG is calculated according to the equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, with T the absolute temperature set up for the ITC experiment.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 ITC thermograms: The ITC thermograms for Peptide 4 and Peptide 3 are shown in Figure 2. The upper panels show the heat flow (μcal/sec) over time (min). The lower panels show the integrated heat (kcal/mol of injectant) as a function of the molar ratio of peptide to Keap1. For Peptide 4, the binding isotherm shows a sigmoidal curve with a plateau at approximately 1.0 molar ratio. For Peptide 3, the binding isotherm also shows a sigmoidal curve with a plateau at approximately 1.0 molar ratio, but the curve is steeper, indicating higher affinity.
